newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK fugitive to arrive to face charges-newspaper.
newsitem.headline: HK fugitive to arrive to face charges-newspaper.

text.p: A Hong Kong fugitive will arrive in the territory on Thursday to face multimillion dollar bribery and conspiracy charges after a long battle to fight extradition from the United States, a newspaper reported.

Jerry Lui Kin-hong, a former tobacco executive, was put on a plane in Boston on Wednesday night after U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright endorsed an order for his extradition, the South China Morning Post said on Thursday.

Lui, 41, was escorted on the flight by an official from Hong Kong's Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC) and will be taken directly to ICAC offices for questioning upon his arrival in the territory, it said.
Lui is expected to face charges of accepting bribes of HK$33 million (US$4.27 million) in connection with a cigarette smuggling syndicate, the newspaper reported.
ICAC officials were not immediately available for comment.
A U.S. federal court in Boston ordered Lui's extradition in March, overturning an earlier ruling by a district court judge who blocked Lui's return.

Boston District Court Judge Joseph Tauro had blocked Lui's extradition after defence lawyers argued that he faced possible execution if forced to return to Hong Kong as his trial was unlikely to be completed before the handover of the colony to Chinese rule on July 1.
Tauro's decision raised a furore in Hong Kong and was seen as undermining efforts to persuade the world it will retain judicial independence after the handover.
